title: AlphaFold 2 at CASP14
claim: our latest AlphaFold system achieves a median score of 92.4 GDT overall across all targets.
context: DeepMind reported this result for AlphaFold 2 in CASP14, an assessment using protein structures withheld from participants before prediction. [1] DeepMind subsequently made AlphaFold 2 inference code and model parameters available in its public repository. [2] The independent ColabFold team reported matching AlphaFold 2 prediction quality on CASP14 targets using AlphaFold 2 with a different sequence-search pipeline. [3] The AlphaFold repository cautions that some CASP14 targets involved manual interventions and that reproducing the competition results requires the original database versions. [2]

title: Whisper's speech recognition release
claim: We’ve trained and are open-sourcing a neural net called Whisper that approaches human level robustness and accuracy on English speech recognition.
context: OpenAI announced Whisper with models and inference code, describing training on 680,000 hours of multilingual audio and acknowledging that it did not outperform specialized models on LibriSpeech. [1] Its public repository supplies transcription code and releases code and model weights under the MIT license. [2] Independent researchers Olivier and Raj evaluated Whisper, finding robustness to random noise but susceptibility to deliberately constructed adversarial audio perturbations. [3] A separate study by Koenecke and colleagues found many accurate transcriptions alongside invented phrases or sentences in roughly 1% of transcriptions in their evaluated sample, with higher hallucination rates for speech containing longer pauses. [4]

title: Segment Anything's zero-shot transfer
claim: The model is designed and trained to be promptable, so it can transfer zero-shot to new image distributions and tasks.
context: Meta's Segment Anything paper introduced a promptable image-segmentation model and a dataset containing over one billion masks on 11 million images. [1] The public SAM repository provides inference code, model checkpoints, example notebooks and an Apache 2.0 license. [2] An independent study by Mazurowski and colleagues evaluated SAM on 19 medical imaging datasets and found that it outperformed several interactive segmentation methods in almost all single-point prompt settings. [3] That study also found substantial variation between tasks, better performance with box prompts than point prompts, and limited or poor performance on some medical datasets. [3]

title: GPT-4's top-decile bar exam claim
claim: it passes a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers
context: OpenAI made this comparison when releasing GPT-4 text capabilities through ChatGPT and an API waitlist. [1] Katz and colleagues reported a simulated Uniform Bar Examination score of approximately 297, above the passing thresholds they considered; their paper acknowledges assistance from OpenAI. [2] Their published discussion places the score between approximately the 68th and 90th percentiles depending on the jurisdiction and exam administration used for comparison. [2] Eric Martínez's re-evaluation replicated the multiple-choice score but challenged the essay grading and comparison population, estimating approximately the 62nd percentile against first-time test takers. [3]

title: Devin's SWE-bench launch result
claim: Devin correctly resolves 13.86%* of the issues end-to-end, far exceeding the previous state-of-the-art of 1.96%.
context: Cognition introduced Devin as an AI software engineer and published demonstrations of coding, debugging and repository maintenance. [1] The launch announcement says its SWE-bench evaluation used a random 25% subset, with Devin unassisted and comparison models given the files to edit. [1] The announcement offered early access through a waitlist rather than unrestricted access. [1] In January 2025, Answer.AI published a hands-on evaluation reporting three successes, fourteen failures and three inconclusive outcomes across twenty tasks, including successful setup work and failures involving existing projects. [2] Answer.AI's tasks were a separate product evaluation rather than a reproduction of Cognition's original SWE-bench experiment. [1][2]

title: Recall's launch privacy promise
claim: You are always in control with privacy you can trust.
context: Microsoft introduced Recall for Copilot+ PCs with a planned June 18, 2024 preview, describing an on-device semantic index, local snapshots, deletion controls and app or website exclusions. [1] On June 7, Microsoft announced explicit opt-in, Windows Hello requirements and additional protection including encryption of the search index database. [2] A June 13 update moved Recall from the planned broad June 18 preview to Windows Insider testing before wider availability. [2] On April 25, 2025, Microsoft announced the public rollout of Recall, still labeled preview, describing opt-in, biometric authentication and isolated processing of encrypted snapshots. [3]

title: Gemini's 2023 multimodal demo
claim: Our natively multimodal AI model Gemini is capable of reasoning across text, images, audio, video and code.
context: Google published this Gemini demonstration video on December 6, 2023; the quoted sentence appears in its video description. [1] The description discloses that latency was reduced and model outputs shortened for the demonstration. [1] Google's accompanying developer article presents image-and-text prompts and model responses used to make the demonstration, including rock-paper-scissors recognition and visual reasoning examples. [2] Tom's Hardware reported Google's explanation that the demonstration used still frames and typed prompts rather than the recorded real-time spoken interaction suggested by its presentation. [3]

title: Galactica's scientific knowledge claim
claim: In this paper we introduce Galactica: a large language model that can store, combine and reason about scientific knowledge.
context: The Galactica paper, submitted on November 16, 2022, reports training on scientific material and benchmark results on scientific question answering, mathematics and other tasks. [1] Meta also released a public web demonstration that could produce literature reviews and other scientific text, according to contemporaneous reporting by Ars Technica. [2] Ars reported that the demonstration generated factual inaccuracies and fabricated scientific material and was taken offline within days of launch. [2] The authors' public repository still provides model-loading instructions and lists five model sizes, so withdrawal of the hosted demonstration did not amount to removal of all access to the models. [3]
